mainTopic: Guarding one's Torah learning, the changing of the לחם הפנים, and what 'לא ימוש' requires
overview: The amud opens with teachings of ריש לקיש about the honor of Torah. He says stopping Torah study can sometimes be its foundation, as when משה broke the לוחות. He also says a תלמיד חכם who sinned is not shamed in public, and that forgetting even one thing from one's learning is a לאו. רבינא counts two לאוין in forgetting, and רב נחמן בר יצחק counts three. The גמרא then limits the rule: it does not cover forgetting through אונס or learning that was too hard. Next, a משנה describes how the לחם הפנים was changed each שבת. It covers the marble and gold tables, eight כהנים sliding the bread on and off, and רבי יוסי's view that a short gap is still 'תמיד'. It also gives what happens when יום כיפורים falls on or before שבת. From רבי יוסי's reading of 'תמיד', the גמרא learns that a little Torah in the morning and evening fulfills 'לא ימוש'. Different views follow on what that פסוק demands. The amud ends with חזקיה's דרשה that הקדוש ברוך הוא lures people from death to life, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sometimes stopping Torah study is what builds it
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his teaching that the 'neglect' of Torah can be its foundation, and proves it from the breaking of the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the neglect of Torah is its foundation, as it says 'which you broke.' ה׳ said to משה: Well done for breaking them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching of ריש לקיש that began just before this section: sometimes putting Torah aside is what builds it up. It brings a proof from משה breaking the first לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the second לוחות says 'אשר שברת', 'which you broke.' The word אשר is read as a hint to יישר כחך, a thank-you from ה׳. Breaking the first לוחות looked like destroying Torah, but it led to the second לוחות. So something that looks like neglect of Torah can really be its foundation.

keyTerms.meaning: Neglect or stopping of Torah study
Well done; literally 'may your strength be upright'
The stone tablets of the Ten Commandments

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that skipping Torah study is generally good. It means that in special cases, stopping for the right reason ends up building Torah, like משה breaking the לוחות.

phrases.english: that the neglect of Torah is its foundation,
as it is written: 'which you broke.'
phrases.notes: שמות 34:1

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Well done that you broke them.
phrases.notes: The word אשר is read as a hint to יישר, so the פסוק is really thanking משה.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבִּיטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה זֶהוּ יִסּוּדָהּ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement of ריש לקיש that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sometimes putting Torah aside is what lays its foundation, as seen from ה׳ praising משה for breaking the לוחות.

steps.title: A Torah scholar who sinned is not shamed in public
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a תלמיד חכם who sinned should not be disgraced publicly, learned from a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: A Torah scholar who sinned is not shamed in public, as it says, 'You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night.' Cover him like the night.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new teaching: if a תלמיד חכם does something wrong, we do not shame him in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the prophet's stumbling to 'night.' ריש לקיש reads this as a lesson: just as night covers things up, we should cover up a scholar's mistake instead of exposing it. This protects the honor of Torah that the scholar represents.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
A Torah scholar who sinned,
we do not disgrace him in public,
as it is said: 'And you will stumble by day,
and the prophet will also stumble with you by night' –
phrases.notes: הושע 4:5

phrases.english: cover him like the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁסָּרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching of ריש לקיש, also about the honor of Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם who sinned is not disgraced in public; his wrongdoing is covered up like the night.

steps.title: Forgetting even one thing from your learning is a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that a person who forgets even one matter of his learning violates a לאו, based on a פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who forgets one thing from his learning violates a prohibition, as it says, 'Guard yourself and guard your soul very much, lest you forget the things.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a third teaching: forgetting even one piece of your Torah learning breaks a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a פסוק that warns us not to forget what we saw at הר סיני. ריש לקיש applies it to anyone who lets his learning slip away. The next step explains why this פסוק counts as a real לאו and not just good advice.

keyTerms.meaning: One who forgets, or lets himself forget

steps.confusionAlert: The word is הַמְשַׁכֵּחַ, which suggests letting oneself forget through not reviewing. It is not talking about a person who forgets because he could not help it.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who forgets one matter from his learning
violates a prohibition,
as it is said: 'Guard yourself and guard your soul very much,
lest you forget the things,'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הַמְשַׁכֵּחַ דָּבָר אֶחָד מִתַּלְמוּדוֹ עוֹבֵר בְּלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of ריש לקיש about protecting one's Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting even one matter of one's learning is a violation of a לאו.

steps.title: Why the פסוק counts as a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains ריש לקיש's ruling with a rule from רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא: השמר, פן and אל always mean a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא, who said: Wherever it says 'guard,' 'lest,' or 'do not,' it is a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up ריש לקיש by explaining why the words of that פסוק create a real prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think 'guard yourself... lest you forget' is only good advice. רבי אילעא's rule says that the words השמר, פן and אל in the Torah always mean a לא תעשה. Since our פסוק uses השמר and פן, forgetting is a true לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used all over the גמרא to decide when a פסוק counts as a לאו.

phrases.english: And this follows what Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a:
Wherever it says 'guard,' 'lest,' or 'do not' –
it is nothing other than a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִדְרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the rule that turns the פסוק in step 3 into a real לאו.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that forgetting one's learning is a לאו
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא: השמר, פן and אל always signal a לא תעשה

steps.title: רבינא: forgetting breaks two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says השמר and פן are two separate לאוין, so forgetting violates two prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: 'Guard' and 'lest' are two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds to ריש לקיש: since the פסוק has two warning words, a person who forgets violates two לאוין, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using רבי אילעא's rule, each warning word counts on its own. The פסוק has both השמר and פן. So רבינא counts two separate prohibitions.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
'Guard' and 'lest' are two prohibitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הִשָּׁמֶר וּפֶן שְׁנֵי לָאוִין נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אילעא's rule to count more than the single לאו ריש לקיש mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgets his learning violates two לאוין: השמר and פן.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: forgetting breaks three prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says forgetting violates three לאוין, counting השמר, ושמור נפשך and פן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He violates three prohibitions, as it says, 'Guard yourself and guard your soul very much, lest you forget the things.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes one step further than רבינא and counts three prohibitions in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He quotes the whole פסוק again to show a third warning word: ושמור נפשך, which comes from the same root as השמר. So he counts השמר, ושמור and פן, which makes three לאוין.
steps.whatToRemember: Forgetting one's Torah learning is a serious matter: ריש לקיש says it is a לאו, רבינא counts two לאוין, and רב נחמן בר יצחק counts three, all from the same פסוק in דברים.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He violates three prohibitions,
as it is said: 'Guard yourself and guard your soul very much,
lest you forget the things.'
phrases.notes: The extra one is 'guard your soul,' which shares a root with 'guard yourself,' so it counts too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third לאו to רבינא's count of two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgets his learning violates three לאוין: השמר, ושמור נפשך and פן.

steps.title: Forgetting only counts when it is by choice
steps.stepSummary: The לאו of forgetting does not apply to someone who forgot because of אונס. It applies only to someone who actively lets the learning leave his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this applies even to someone who forgot because of something beyond his control. So the פסוק says, 'And lest they depart from your heart.' The פסוק is talking about someone who removes them from his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows ריש לקיש's rule about forgetting. It shows from the פסוק that the לאו is only for someone who lets his learning go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'lest they depart from your heart' describe something the person himself allows to happen. So a person who forgot because of illness, trouble or other forces outside his control is not included. The rule stays a לאו, but its scope is now limited.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' — introduces a possible mistaken reading that the פסוק will correct
'The verse teaches' — introduces the פסוק that settles the question
'The verse is speaking about' — defines who the פסוק is aimed at

phrases.english: One might think: even because of his being forced?
phrases.notes: He means even someone who forgot because of something he couldn't help.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'And lest they depart from your heart' –
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: about one who removes them from his heart
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מֵחֲמַת אוֹנְסוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the לאוין of forgetting counted in steps 3–6 so that they cover only forgetting by choice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting caused by אונס is not included in the לאו; only someone who lets the learning leave his heart is included.

steps.title: Learning that was too hard is also excluded
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי בר רבי ינאי adds that someone whose learning was too difficult for him to hold on to is also not included, learned from the word 'רק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי, son of רבי ינאי, says: You might think this applies even if his learning was too hard for him. So the פסוק says, 'Only.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage adds another exclusion from the לאו of forgetting, based on the first word of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'רק' ('only') is read as narrowing the rule. If the material was simply too hard for this person to keep, he is not punished for forgetting it. Together with step 7, this means the לאו covers only forgetting caused by neglect.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning was too hard for him, literally 'his learning overpowered him'
'Only' — a word read as limiting the scope of the rule

steps.whatToRemember: The לאו of forgetting Torah is only for someone who lets it slip away through neglect. It does not cover forgetting from אונס or from learning that was too difficult.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai says:
One might think: even if his learning was too hard for him?
The verse teaches: 'Only.'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק opens with 'רק השמר לך,' and that 'only' cuts down who is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ תָּקְפָה עָלָיו מִשְׁנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exclusion alongside the אונס exclusion of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone whose learning was too difficult to retain is excluded from the לאו, learned from 'רק'.

steps.title: Torah and the soul both formed in forty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר link Torah, given in forty days, with the soul, formed in forty days. Whoever guards his Torah has his soul guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: The Torah was given in forty days, and the soul is formed in forty days. Whoever guards his Torah, his soul is guarded. Whoever does not guard the Torah, his soul is not guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: Two sages share an אגדה that shows how serious forgetting Torah is. They do it by connecting Torah to the soul through the number forty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both Torah and the soul are tied to the number forty, they are linked. Taking care of one is taking care of the other. This explains why neglecting Torah is treated so severely in the steps before.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both say:
The Torah was given in forty,
phrases.notes: Forty days, the time משה spent on the mountain.

phrases.english: and the soul is formed in forty.
Anyone who guards his Torah –
his soul is guarded,
and anyone who does not guard the Torah –
his soul is not guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal details of the לאו to an אגדה about how serious it is to neglect Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guarding one's Torah means one's soul is guarded; neglecting Torah means the soul is not guarded.

steps.title: The parable of the bird given to a servant
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל compares this to a master who hands his servant a cheap bird and warns him that losing it will cost his life, not just its small price.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: It is like a man who handed a sparrow to his servant. He said: Do you think that if you lose it, I will take from you an איסר, its value? I will take your soul from you!
steps.whatsHappening: A parable backs up the idea from step 9 that losing Torah puts one's soul at stake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird is worth only a tiny coin, but the master says losing it costs the servant his life. In the same way, Torah entrusted to a person is not something he can lose cheaply. Neglecting it carries the most serious result.

keyTerms.meaning: A sparrow, a small free-flying bird
A small coin of low value

steps.whatToRemember: Torah given to a person is like a trust held for the Master. Losing it through neglect puts the soul itself at stake.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
A parable: it is like a person
who handed a sparrow to his servant,
and said: Do you imagine
that if you lose it
I will take from you an issar as its value?
phrases.notes: An איסר is a tiny coin, about what such a bird is worth.

phrases.english: I will take your soul from you!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁמָּסַר צִפּוֹר דְּרוֹר לְעַבְדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 9's teaching that neglecting Torah puts the soul at risk.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that failing to guard Torah puts one's soul at risk
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable from the school of רבי ישמעאל about a master, a servant and a sparrow

steps.title: Two tables in the entrance hall for the showbread
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: two tables, one marble and one gold, stood inside the אולם by the entrance to the היכל. The new לחם הפנים was placed on the marble one before going in, and the old לחם הפנים on the gold one after coming out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two tables in the אולם, on the inside, at the entrance to the היכל. One was of marble and one was of gold. On the marble one they place the לחם הפנים when it is brought in, and on the gold one when it is taken out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes two tables near the entrance to the היכל that were used when changing the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new loaves rested on the marble table on their way in. The old loaves rested on the gold table on their way out. The next step gives the reason for using the gold table on the way out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה — marks the start of a new משנה
The entrance hall in front of the היכל in the בית המקדש
The showbread, twelve loaves kept on the שולחן in the היכל

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There were two tables in the entrance hall, on the inside,
at the entrance of the House,
phrases.notes: 'The House' here means the היכל, the main sanctuary building.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁל שַׁיִישׁ וְאֶחָד שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: one of marble and one of gold.

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁל שַׁיִישׁ נוֹתְנִים לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ,
phrases.english: On the marble one they place the showbread when it is brought in,
and on the gold one when it is taken out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנֵי שׁוּלְחָנוֹת הָיוּ בָּאוּלָם מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about forgetting Torah and opens a new משנה about the לחם הפנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new לחם הפנים is placed on a marble table before entering the היכל, and the old לחם הפנים on a gold table after leaving it.

steps.title: Why the old bread goes on a gold table, and the gold table inside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains why the old לחם הפנים is placed on a gold table on its way out: מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. It then mentions the main gold שולחן inside the היכל, where the bread always rests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because in holy matters we go up and do not go down. And there was one gold table inside, on which the לחם הפנים always lay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its description of the tables from Step 11. It gives the reason for using the gold table on the way out, and then names the main gold table inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All week the bread sat on the gold שולחן inside. Putting it on a marble table on the way out would lower its level, so it goes onto the gold table in the אולם instead. The משנה gives a reason only for the gold table on the way out. It gives no reason here for using marble on the way in.

keyTerms.meaning: In holy matters we raise the level and never lower it
Inside, meaning in the היכל itself

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין is a general principle that shows up in many places across ש״ס, not only here.

phrases.english: because in holy matters we go up and do not go down.
phrases.notes: This is the reason the old bread from Step 11 goes onto the gold table, not the marble one, on its way out.

phrases.english: And there was one table of gold inside,
on which the shewbread always lay.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמַּעֲלִין בַּקּוֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא מוֹרִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה from Step 11 by giving the reason for the gold table on the way out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The old לחם הפנים goes onto a gold table when it comes out, because holiness may be raised but never lowered. The main gold שולחן inside always holds the bread.

steps.title: Eight priests take part in the bread switch
steps.stepSummary: Four כהנים come in carrying the two new stacks of bread and the two בזיכין of frankincense. Four other כהנים go in ahead of them to take off the old stacks and the old בזיכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four כהנים enter: two hold the two stacks of bread and two hold the two בזיכין. Four more go in before them: two to take the two old stacks and two to take the two old בזיכין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now describes who does the switch. Four כהנים bring the new items in, and four go in first to take the old items out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stacks of bread and two cups of frankincense, so each item needs its own כהן both coming and going. The removers go in first so that they are already in position when the new bread arrives. This sets up the exact switching method in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Stacks or arrangements; the bread was set in two stacks of six loaves
Small cups holding the frankincense (לבונה) placed with the bread
Go in ahead of, arrive first

phrases.english: And four priests enter:
two with the two stacks of bread in their hands,
and two with the two bowls of frankincense in their hands.
And four priests go in before them:
two to take the two stacks,
and two to take the two bowls.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְבָּעָה כֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the tables to the people who carry out the switch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight כהנים take part: four bring in the new bread and frankincense, and four who enter first remove the old.

steps.title: Sliding the bread so the table is never empty
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים bringing in the bread stand on the north side and the ones removing it stand on the south. As each handbreadth of old bread is pulled off, a handbreadth of new bread is slid on, because the פסוק says 'לפני תמיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ones bringing in stand in the north facing south, and the ones taking out stand in the south facing north. These pull and those set down, one handbreadth of this one opposite one handbreadth of that one, as it says: 'before Me always.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes exactly how the switch is done. The old bread slides off as the new bread slides on, so there is never a moment with no bread on the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two groups stand on opposite sides of the שולחן, facing each other. The handbreadth-for-handbreadth method keeps some bread on the table the whole time. The source is the word 'תמיד', which the תנא קמא reads as 'with no break at all'.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a small unit of length

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate things happen here: the old bread is pulled off and the new bread is slid on at the same moment. It is not done as two steps one after the other.

phrases.english: Those bringing in the new bread stand in the north,
and their faces are to the south,
and those taking out the old bread stand in the south,
and their faces are to the north.
These pull the old bread off, and those set the new bread down,

phrases.aramaic: וְטִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד טִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: a handbreadth of this one matching a handbreadth of that one,
phrases.notes: Every bit of old bread that slides off is replaced right away by the same amount of new bread.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'before Me always.'
phrases.notes: שמות 25:30

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּכְנִיסִים עוֹמְדִים בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the eight כהנים from Step 13 actually carry out the switch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new bread must be slid on as the old bread slides off, handbreadth for handbreadth, so the שולחן is never without bread, based on 'לפני תמיד'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a short gap is still 'always'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with the תנא קמא. Even if the old bread is taken off completely first and the new bread is set down afterward, that still counts as 'תמיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even if these take off and then those set down, that too is 'always'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dissenting opinion. רבי יוסי says the bread does not have to be swapped with no break at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about what the word 'תמיד' requires. The תנא קמא says it means no gap at all, which is why the bread must be slid handbreadth for handbreadth. רבי יוסי says the bread can be taken off first and the new bread put down afterward, and the word 'תמיד' is still kept.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא reads 'תמיד' as no gap even for a moment, so the bread is swapped handbreadth for handbreadth. רבי יוסי says taking off first and then setting down is also 'תמיד'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument about what 'תמיד' means sets up the discussion that follows in the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if these take off, and only then those set down,
that too would count as 'always.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵלּוּ נוֹטְלִין וְאֵלּוּ מַנִּיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's strict reading of 'תמיד' in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, taking off the old bread first and then setting down the new bread still fulfills 'לפני תמיד'.

steps.title: The old bread goes out, the frankincense is burned, and the loaves are shared
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים carry the old לחם הפנים out to the gold table in the אולם. They burn the frankincense from the בזיכין, and then the loaves are divided among the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came out and put the old loaves on the gold table in the אולם. They burned the frankincense from the bowls, and the loaves were divided among the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the process of changing the bread by telling us what happens to the old loaves after they leave the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old bread may not be eaten until its frankincense is burned. The burning of the בזיכין is what allows the כהנים to eat the bread. Only after that are the loaves shared out.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold table standing in the אולם, where the old bread is placed on its way out

phrases.english: They came out and placed them
on the gold table that was in the Entrance Hall,
they burned the bowls,
phrases.notes: It means the frankincense inside the bowls, not the bowls themselves.

phrases.english: and the loaves are divided among the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְאוּ וּנְתָנוּם עַל שֻׁלְחָן הַזָּהָב שֶׁהָיָה בָּאוּלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's step-by-step description of changing the לחם הפנים. Steps 11-12 already told us the old bread goes onto the gold table in the אולם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the old bread is placed on the gold table in the אולם, the frankincense is burned, and then the loaves are divided among the כהנים.

steps.title: When יום כיפורים falls on שבת, the bread is shared at night
steps.stepSummary: If יום כיפורים falls on שבת, the old loaves are still removed that day, but they are shared out only at night, after the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יום כיפורים falls on שבת, the loaves are divided at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a calendar problem: the bread is changed on שבת, but this time שבת is also a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the bread still happens on שבת as usual. Since nobody may eat on יום כיפורים, the sharing of the loaves waits until the fast ends that night.

phrases.english: If Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat,
the loaves are divided at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל יוֹם כִּיפּוּרִים לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule just stated, that the loaves are divided among the כהנים, and applies it to the special case where שבת is יום כיפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום כיפורים is on שבת, the לחם הפנים is divided only at night, after the fast.

steps.title: When יום כיפורים falls on Friday, the goat is eaten Friday night, even raw
steps.stepSummary: If יום כיפורים falls on ערב שבת, the meat of the שעיר of יום כיפורים must be eaten that night. Since it cannot be cooked, the Babylonian כהנים eat it raw, because they are not fussy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it falls on Friday, the goat of יום כיפורים is eaten at night. The Babylonians eat it raw, because they are not fussy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second calendar problem, this time about the meat of the יום כיפורים goat offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat's meat can be eaten only that day and the following night. On Friday the כהנים are fasting, and on Friday night it is already שבת, so there is no chance to cook it. The משנה notes that the Babylonian כהנים simply ate it raw.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat brought as a חטאת on יום כיפורים, whose meat the כהנים eat
Literally 'their mind is pleasant'; they are not fussy about their food

steps.confusionAlert: 'Eaten at night' means Friday night, right after the fast ends. It is not the night when יום כיפורים begins. By Friday night it is already שבת, which is why the meat cannot be cooked.

phrases.english: If it occurs on Shabbat eve,
phrases.notes: 'It' is יום כיפורים, still the subject from the line before.

phrases.english: the goat of Yom Kippur
is eaten at night,
and the Babylonians eat it when it is raw,
because they are not particular.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second calendar case in the same pattern as step 17, about when יום כיפורים falls near שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום כיפורים is on Friday, the שעיר is eaten Friday night. Since it cannot be cooked, the Babylonian כהנים eat it raw.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the table only must not stay empty overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי goes further than in the משנה. Even if the old bread is removed in the morning and the new bread is placed only in the evening, nothing is wrong. 'לפני תמיד' only means the table may not be left overnight without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, even if he removed the old bread in the morning and set out the new bread in the evening, there is nothing wrong with that. So how do I fulfill 'before Me always'? The table must not be left overnight without bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by bringing a ברייתא that shows how far רבי יוסי's view in the משנה (step 15) really goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי only allowed a short gap between taking off the old bread and putting on the new. Here he allows the table to be empty for most of the day. For him, 'תמיד' simply means the table is never empty through a night.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the חכמים that explains the משנה
'Before Me always', the פסוק's requirement for the לחם הפנים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי אמי's lesson in the next step. If 'תמיד' can mean 'once in the morning and once in the evening,' the same reading can apply to other מצוות described as 'always.'

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei says,
even if he removed the old bread in the morning
and arranged the new bread in the evening,
there is nothing wrong with that.
Rather, how do I fulfill 'before Me always'?
phrases.notes: שמות 25:30

phrases.english: That the table should not be left overnight without bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִילּוּ סִילֵּק אֶת הַיְּשָׁנָה שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוסי's view in the משנה (step 15) and shows from a ברייתא that he allows an even longer gap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, 'לפני תמיד' only requires that the שולחן not stay overnight without bread. Removing the old bread in the morning and setting out the new in the evening is fine.

steps.title: רבי אמי: one chapter morning and evening fulfills 'it shall not depart from your mouth'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי learns from רבי יוסי that 'always' can be fulfilled once in the morning and once in the evening. So a person who learns just one פרק in the morning and one in the evening fulfills the מצוה of 'לא ימוש ספר התורה הזה מפיך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: From רבי יוסי's words we learn that even if a person learned only one chapter in the morning and one chapter in the evening, he has fulfilled the מצוה of 'This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי takes רבי יוסי's reading of 'תמיד' about the לחם הפנים and applies it to the מצוה of learning Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, 'always' means there is no empty night, not a nonstop presence. In the same way, 'day and night' learning can be met by a bit of learning in the morning and a bit in the evening. רבי אמי is using רבי יוסי's reasoning in a new area.

keyTerms.meaning: We may learn, we can derive

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי reads 'תמיד' as 'never left empty overnight,' not 'every single moment.' רבי אמי uses this to teach that one פרק in the morning and one in the evening fulfills 'לא ימוש.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
From the words of Rabbi Yosei we may learn
that even if a person learned only
one chapter in the morning
and one chapter in the evening,
he has fulfilled the מצוה of
'This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:8. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the principle from רבי יוסי's ברייתא (step 19) and applies it to the מצוה of learning Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning one פרק in the morning and one in the evening fulfills 'לא ימוש ספר התורה הזה מפיך,' following רבי יוסי's reading of 'תמיד.'

steps.title: שמע morning and evening fulfills 'Shall not depart'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says that saying only קריאת שמע in the morning and evening fulfills 'לא ימוש.' But this must not be said in front of עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Even if a person read only קריאת שמע in the morning and evening, he has kept 'לא ימוש.' But it is forbidden to say this in front of עמי הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that goes even further than רבי אמי. Just saying קריאת שמע twice a day counts as keeping 'לא ימוש.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי needed one פרק of learning in the morning and one at night. רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the two daily קריאת שמע are already enough. The warning about עמי הארץ is there because simple people might think they never need to learn more.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying the שמע, done every morning and evening
Unlearned people who are not careful about Torah

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
Even if a person read nothing
except the recitation of Shema morning and evening,
he has fulfilled 'shall not depart,'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from the last step: 'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth' (יהושע 1:8).

phrases.english: and this matter is forbidden to say
in front of ignorant people,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אמי's idea of morning and evening as 'always' to just קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קריאת שמע morning and evening fulfills 'לא ימוש,' but this should not be told to עמי הארץ.

steps.title: רבא says it is a מצוה to tell the ignorant
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees about the warning. He says it is a מצוה to tell this to עמי הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: It is a מצוה to say it in front of עמי הארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view on whether to share this teaching with simple people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue about the הלכה itself. He argues only about how to teach it. Telling simple people how much even שמע is worth can encourage them, since they will see how much more full learning is worth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to say it

phrases.english: And Rava said:
It is a מצוה to say it in front of ignorant people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִצְוָה לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the restriction at the end of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is a מצוה to tell עמי הארץ that קריאת שמע fulfills 'לא ימוש.'

steps.title: בן דמה asks about studying Greek wisdom
steps.stepSummary: בן דמה, the nephew of רבי ישמעאל, has learned the whole Torah. He asks whether he may now study חכמת יוונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן דמה, son of רבי ישמעאל's sister, asked רבי ישמעאל: Someone like me, who has learned the entire Torah, may he study Greek wisdom?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts with a question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן דמה thinks that once he has 'finished' the Torah, his duty is done and he has free time. The question tests how far the duty of 'לא ימוש' goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Greek wisdom, meaning outside, non-Torah learning
What is the law? Is it allowed?

phrases.english: Ben Dama asked,
the son of Rabbi Yishmael's sister,
Rabbi Yishmael:
Someone like me, who has learned
the entire Torah,
what is the law about studying Greek wisdom?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל בֶּן דָּמָה, בֶּן אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that also uses the פסוק 'לא ימוש.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether someone who has learned the whole Torah may study חכמת יוונית.

steps.title: Find an hour that is neither day nor night
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers with the פסוק 'והגית בו יומם ולילה.' Since Torah fills all day and all night, there is no free time left for Greek wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read this פסוק to him: 'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall think about it day and night.' Go find an hour that is neither day nor night, and study Greek wisdom then.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers בן דמה. He sends him to look for a time that does not exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads 'day and night' as every moment, not just morning and evening. Since no hour is outside day and night, the answer really means no. This reading is stricter than רבי שמעון בן יוחי in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall think about it, meaning study it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל is not really giving permission. He is answering with a riddle, and the riddle means there is no such hour.

phrases.english: He read this verse about him:
'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth,
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:8

phrases.english: and you shall think about it day and night.'
Go and search for an hour
that is not part of the day
and not part of the night,
and study Greek wisdom in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרָא עָלָיו הַמִּקְרָא הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בן דמה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah study must fill every hour of day and night, so there is no time left for חכמת יוונית.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: the פסוק is a blessing, not a command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי ישמעאל's reading argues with רבי יונתן. רבי יונתן says the פסוק 'לא ימוש' is not a חובה or a מצוה, but a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי שמואל בר נחמני, who said in the name of רבי יונתן: This פסוק is not a duty and not a מצוה, but a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a disagreement. רבי יונתן does not read 'לא ימוש' as a command at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל used the פסוק as a rule that forbids Greek wisdom. If the פסוק is only a ברכה, that rule falls away. The next step shows where רבי יונתן gets this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A blessing, a promise rather than a command

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani,
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבי ישמעאל's answer to בן דמה.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
This verse is not a duty
and not a מצוה, but a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an opinion that argues with רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא ימוש' is a ברכה, not a חובה or a מצוה.

steps.title: ה׳ blesses יהושע for loving Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains his reading. ה׳ saw that יהושע loved Torah and never left the אהל, so He blessed him that Torah would never leave his mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הקדוש ברוך הוא saw that יהושע loved Torah very much, as it says: 'His servant יהושע בן נון, a young man, did not leave the tent.' ה׳ said to him: יהושע, is Torah so dear to you? 'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the support for רבי יונתן. It uses an earlier פסוק to show that 'לא ימוש' was a reward for יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, 'לא ימיש,' describes יהושע never leaving the tent of Torah. So 'לא ימוש' to him reads as a matching blessing, measure for measure, and not as a new command.

keyTerms.meaning: The tent where משה learned with ה׳

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, saw Joshua
that words of Torah were very dear to him,
as it says:
'And his servant Joshua son of Nun, a young man,
phrases.notes: שמות 33:11

phrases.english: did not leave the tent.'
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, כׇּל כָּךְ חֲבִיבִין עָלֶיךָ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה?
phrases.english: Joshua, are words of Torah so dear to you?
'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth.'
phrases.notes: Here ה׳ says the פסוק as a blessing: since you love Torah, it will always stay with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יונתן calls the פסוק a ברכה.
steps.raayaObject: That 'לא ימוש' is a ברכה, not a command.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 33:11, which says יהושע 'לא ימיש מתוך האהל.'

steps.title: Torah is not a burden, but you cannot exempt yourself
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches a balance. Torah should not feel like a heavy duty, yet a person may not free himself from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Words of Torah should not be a burden on you, and you are not allowed to free yourself from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the topic with a balanced teaching about how to relate to Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This joins the two sides. Torah should not feel like a forced tax that you pay and finish. But it is also not optional, so no one may excuse himself from learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
To free yourself, to exempt yourself

steps.whatToRemember: There are several views of 'לא ימוש.' רבי שמעון בן יוחי says קריאת שמע twice a day is enough. רבי ישמעאל says every hour, so there is no time for חכמת יוונית. רבי יונתן says it is a ברכה to יהושע. The final balance is that Torah should not feel like a burden, but you may never exempt yourself from it.

phrases.english: Words of Torah should not be a burden on you,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of 'לא ימוש' with a balanced teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah should not be treated as a burden, but no one may exempt himself from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Learn Torah out of love, not as a debt, yet never consider yourself free from it.

steps.title: חזקיה opens a דרשה on a פסוק in איוב
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה opens a new teaching by asking for the meaning of the פסוק 'ואף הסיתך מפי צר רחב לא מוצק תחתיה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: What is the meaning of the verse, 'And also He has drawn you out of a narrow mouth, to a broad place with no narrowness beneath it'?
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה quotes a פסוק from איוב and asks what it means. This is a setup line: the גמרא is getting ready to give his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מאי דכתיב' show that a fresh דרשה is about to come. The key word to watch is הסיתך, 'He drew you' or 'He lured you.' The next steps build the whole lesson around it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? This opens an explanation of a פסוק.
He lured you, or He drew you away

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And also He has drawn you out of a narrow mouth,
phrases.notes: איוב 36:16

phrases.english: to a broad place with no narrowness beneath it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new אגדה teaching after the discussion of רבי ישמעאל and רבי יונתן on Torah study.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the פסוק 'ואף הסיתך מפי צר רחב לא מוצק תחתיה.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה opens a דרשה on 'ואף הסיתך מפי צר רחב לא מוצק תחתיה', and steps 29-30 explain it.

steps.title: People lure toward death, God lures toward life
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה contrasts the way of human beings with the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. People lure each other from life to death, while הקדוש ברוך הוא lures people from death to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see that the way of בשר ודם is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. The way of בשר ודם is that a person lures his friend from the paths of life to the paths of death. But הקדוש ברוך הוא lures a person from the paths of death to the paths of life.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה states his main idea. Usually 'luring' someone is a bad thing, but when הקדוש ברוך הוא does it, it leads a person to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere in the Torah, the word מסית means someone who leads a friend toward sin. חזקיה flips the picture: הקדוש ברוך הוא is also a 'מסית,' but He pulls in the opposite direction, toward life. That is why the פסוק uses the word הסיתך.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see. This introduces a lesson or contrast.
a way of acting or behavior
flesh and blood, meaning human beings
paths of life and paths of death

steps.confusionAlert: Here מסית does not mean the sinful 'enticer' to idol worship. It is simply the verb 'to lure' or 'to draw,' used for God leading a person toward good.

phrases.english: Come and see

The way of flesh and blood:
a person lures his friend

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the central idea that answers the question about the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person lures others from life to death, but הקדוש ברוך הוא lures a person from death to life.

steps.title: The narrow mouth is the opening of גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה proves his point from the פסוק. 'Out of a narrow mouth' means out of גיהנם, whose opening is narrow so that its smoke stays gathered inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is said: 'And also He has drawn you out of a narrow mouth.' This means from גיהנם, whose mouth is narrow so that its smoke stays gathered in.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה links his idea back to the words of the פסוק. The 'narrow mouth' that God pulls a person out of is גיהנם, the 'path of death.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'narrow mouth' is read as גיהנם, the פסוק fits his lesson exactly. הקדוש ברוך הוא lures a person out of death and into the 'broad place' of life. He explains that גיהנם's mouth is narrow to keep its smoke trapped, and this explanation continues in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said. This introduces a proof from a פסוק.

steps.raayaObject: The claim that הקדוש ברוך הוא lures a person from the paths of death to the paths of life.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 36:16, 'ואף הסיתך מפי צר,' read as being drawn out of the narrow mouth of גיהנם.
